reversed.description: The Queen of Rings might indicate a focus on material matters to the detriment of emotional or personal care.

upright.tags: Abundance, leadership, stability, prosperity, authority, success, solidity, reliability
upright.description: The King of Rings represents success, financial security, and a commanding presence in the material realm.

reversed.tags: Tyranny, stubbornness, poor financial decisions, mismanagement, rigidity, avarice, risk, imprudence
reversed.description: The King of Rings warns of mismanagement of resources or an overemphasis on material control.

upright.tags: The Water Bearer, The Clouds, The Pot, Numbers 11 and 2, Uranus, Air, Wonder, Travel, "The Star"
upright.description:
The eleventh sign of the zodiac, Aquarius is a fixed air sign ruled by the planet Uranus, and in the body is associated with the circulatory system, calves and ankles. In tarot, Aquarius is related to "The Star", and much like "the Star", it seeks adventure, new experiences, and sacred knowledge with an air of optimism. The water-bearer is a traveler both physically and mentally, exploring new vistas and ideas.

Aquarius, ever the rebel, is struck by wanderlust and regards satiating its own curiosity as a top priority. It concerns itself with passion, progress, and knowledge. This card may also suggest that we need to be aware of our ambitions and attempt to keep ourselves in line with reality.

upright.tags: Haloed Light, Smoke, Numbers 32 and 5, Completion, Actualization
upright.description:
The tendrils of Apotheosis envelop the figure, gently wrapping about the body, leaving its eyes clear and unobscured as the light illuminates all that surrounds it. The halo around the head symbolizes the heightening of our consciousness. This card explores the need for clarity, completion, and self-reliance. The conscience has found itself in an elevated state, and slowly we work toward the ever-evolving apex of who we are.
This card encourages us to pursue our highest and most realized selves and expand our mental horizons. Inversely, it can suggest spiritual and mental obstacles are stopping us from reaching our full potential.

upright.tags: The Flame, The Head, Number 1, Mars, Fire, The Ram, Vitality, Beginnings, Power, "The Magician"
upright.description:
The first sign of the zodiac, Ares, is a cardinal fire sign. Associated with fortitude and the manifestation of new ideas, Ares brings with it the ability to take on new tasks zealously and with great ambition. In this deck, Ares is most closely associated with "The Magician" tarot card. Ares is ruled by the planet Mars and governs the head, and while it burns bright, it's energy can be temperamental if not honed and aimed carefully. It can be prone to fizzling out before seeing things through to completion - much like a candle. 

Ares symbolizes novelty, creativity, fast-moving projects, drive, and valour. It can also imply shortsightedness, overextending oneself, rash behavior and other fleeting instincts.

upright.tags: Caucasus Beetle, Wood Apple, Daggers, Numbers 18. 10 and 1, Protection, Withdrawl, Solace, Isolation
upright.description: Protection and boundaries are deeply necessary when leading a grounded life. However, some barriers can operate to our detriment, causing us to push ourselves away from others or isolate ourselves. What things do we seek protection from? What facets of ourselves do we hide away? What is the nature of our boundaries? At what times do we need to pull back, seek solace, and reorient ourselves without the input of others? This card explores the nature of peace, protection, and isolation. It can suggest a need to reinforce one's space and peace, a struggle for independence and privacy, or imply that an individual is withdrawing away from others and the world.

upright.tags: Sunflowers, Numbers 42 and 6, The Sun, Optimisim, Warmth
upright.description: The figure depicted in the Blooms card stands straight, noble, and proud. This card encourages us to take note of the things that are growing around us - what has been sown, and what has been reaped. It is important to recognize the effort that goes into a successful harvest, and be grateful for the collaboration, patience, and love needed in order to help our ambitions flourish. Blooms asks us to be grateful, gracious, and mindful of all the hard work that has been done, and that that remains to be done. It can also imply foolhardy optimism and biting off more than one can chew.

upright.tags: The Moon, The Stromach, Water, Number 4, Inuitation, Compassion, "The Moon", "The High Priestess"
upright.description:
The fourth sign of the zodiac, Cancer is a cardinal water sigh and is affiliated with the stomach, chest, womb and the midsection. Cancer is a deeply intuitive card, able to move between two worlds (the water and the earth). However, it is also prone to "wading" through self imposes melancholy. Cancer is associated with "The Moon" and the "The High Priestess", both cards governed by its ruling planet, the moon.

Cancer encourages us to pay attention to our gut instincts, see past the illusions of this world, pay heed to our emotions, and nurture and protect that which we cherish. It can also imply a near-smothering nature, over-sensitivity, and hyper-vigilance.

upright.tags: The Hourglass, The Scroll, Numbers 10 and 1, Saturn, "The Devil", "The World"
upright.description:
The tenth sign of the zodiac, Capricorn is a cardinal earth sign known to rule the skeletal system and joints. Capricorn is also commonly associated with the planet Saturn, and "The Devil" and "The World" in tarot. Much like the skeletal system, Capricorn prides itself on being the foundation of a strong and capable form. Being the tenth sign of the zodiac, Capricorn finds itself towards the end of the astrological cycle. As the sand within the hourglass falls upon Capricorn, it remains undeterred. This card is studious, rigorous, and almost serene.

Capricorn requests we dig our heels in and do the hard work of acknowledging that while we may not have all the time in the world, we must make the most of what time we have.

upright.tags: The Jago, The Dancers, Numbers 36 and 9, Momentum, Bliss, Awakening
upright.description: In Punjabi marriage rituals, the jago ceremony is a prelude to the main events, symbolized by an earthenware pot decorated with candles. Carried atop the heads of the dancers, the word "jago" literally translate to "awaken" as family members traditionally go from home to home in their villages, awakening members in the early morning to alert them to a marriage being set. The dancers here are present to notify us of new phases in our lives, and bring with them their motion, songs, and joy. This card encourages us to awaken, be blissful, and express gratitude for our many evolutions. It can also suggest momentum, and very fast-paced change.

upright.tags: The Lotus, The Daggers, The Eye, Numbers 23 and 5, Introspection, Patience, Guidance
upright.description: The Disciple sits upon the clouds with their right hand raised in a banishment gesture, while a lotus is cupped in their other palm. This figure seeks wisdom and guidance as they gaze inward and beyond, hoping to see past the illusions of this world. However, The Disciple is not untethered from the earth, as indicated by the lotus on their person. The student sees all things, material and immaterial, and the place they occupy in the greater universe. This card concerns itself with learning, patience, and an even temperament. It can also imply a need to stop oneself from completely disconnecting from the world, and to seek new mentors in the form of divinity, individuals, and the elements.

upright.tags: Candles, Death's-Head Moth, Numbers 48 - 12 - and 3, Death and Rebirth
upright.description: Divinity burns, righteous. Fire is a life-giving element, but it us just as capable of taking it away. Divinity asks us questions about what makes this life precious and fragile. The death's-head moth is delicate, hovering on the precipice between life and death. What powers operating outside of our control lend meaning to our lives and the universe? What do we exalt? To whom do we pray? The games the universe seems to play with us are confusing at times, and they can feel unavoidable. This card suggests a need for broadening one's perspective to see the sacred in all forms of life around us. It also suggests larger forces at constant play.

upright.tags: The Fire, Numbers 27 and 9, Anger, Despair, Discord
upright.description: Effigies in the traditional sense are crude impersonations of a despised person made of straw, fabric, or any other materials. These creations are then burned or abused - typically to express displeasure with the person in question. This card asks us questions about our frustration and anger: is it narrowed and specific? Are signs pointing to a distinct person or circumstance? Do we find ourselves the subject of vitriol in another's eyes? What forces are at play that manipulate our emotions? The Effigy implies frustration, fury, and pointed dislike or despair. It can also signal misdirected anger, breakdowns in communication, and making an idol of one's fury.

upright.tags: Sacred Fig Tree, Clouds, Numbers 33 and 6, Evolution, Transformation, Connection
upright.description: The sacred fig is a tree that has long been associated with divinity, and here it is pictured not in the ground, but floating above, its roots entwined with the clouds. Eternity moves, forward and backward, stretching on into infinity and deeply connected to all that operates withing it. While things do not entirely disappear, they do transform, and much like us evolve into something new. The sacred fig is a life-giver, but also a teacher, and its slow, steady transformation reminds us that not all growth is immediately visible. This card wants us to interrogate our relationship to what we consider permanent. On a long enough timeline, all things grow, decay, and change.

upright.tags: Stars, Light, The Child, Numbers 29 - 11 - and 2, Curiousity, Authority, The Elements of Air and Fire,
upright.description: The paternal figures in The Father and The Mother operate as sort of symbolic portal - the passages by which consciousness enters the world. The figure of The Father cradles a child in its arms whilst reaching up toward the stars, enshrouded by clouds. This card is associated with the elements of air and fire, and relays the need for wisdom, curiosity, and sanctuary. This card can imply a need to expand one's horizons, explore new fascinations and ideas, and a desire to feel protected doing so. Inversely, it can also suggest struggling with authority and feeling stifled.

upright.tags: The Scythes, The Barred Gate, Numbers 18 and 9, Barriers, Boundraries, Obstacles
upright.description: The Gate preoccupies itself with obstacles, boundaries, and barriers. This card asks us questions about the circumstances that block the way forward. Before a gate stand two figures, their scythes crossed, implying some of our hurdles to entry can also be deadly or formidable in nature. What gates and boundaries do we establish to keep ourselves safe? What thresholds must we cross in order to grow and make ourselves anew? What holds us back? This card asks us to pay attention to the barriers we erect around ourselves and our opportunities, and the obstacles in our way. It can also imply hiding, stalling, or an inability to move forward.

upright.tags: The Twins, The Arms, The Clouds, Number 3, Mercury, Air, Duality, "The Lovers" , "The Devil"
upright.description:
The third sign of the zodiac, Gemini is a mutable air sign ruled by the planet Mercury. It is associated with communication, duality of thought, and the pursuit of knowledge. Gemini rules the arms, hands, and nervous system. It seeks to reach out, touch, and understand the world on its own merits, through its own experiences and means. Gemini is associated with both "The Lovers" and "The Devil" in tarot - both which feature the same two figures, entwined, whether it through devotion or vice.

Gemini explores dichotomies in thought, curiosity, and the ability to parse extreme highs and lows. It can also be associated with duplicity, deceit, and masking one's true emotions or intentions.

upright.tags: The Bee, Honeycomb, Numbers 21 and 3, Rhythm, Divine Plans
upright.description:
Harmony is a card that asks us to interrogate our relationship with order, structure, and rhythm. There are specific patterns and harmonies we find ourselves falling into that create the framework and structure of our lives - much like the bees in their hives that operate seamlessly and instinctively. What is our relationship with order? What machinations operate in the background of our lives? 
This card can imply a need to reevaluate habits and take note of what actions are more or less harmonious in our lives. It can also suggest overbearing authority, anxiety, hostility, and friction.

upright.tags: Dagger, Swan, Tigers Head, Clouds, Numbeers 45 and 9, Defense, The Element of Air
upright.description: The Knife signifies action, pain, conflict, intellect, and ambition. The fabricated tigers jaws close around the head of the swan on the handle of the dagger, emphasizing the nature of strife and calm acceptance. A knife can be used both as a tool and a weapon, and this duality emphasizes the ways we can wield power.Do we aim to destroy or build? To protect or harm? This card explores the nature of power, struggle, protection, and ambition. It can also imply violence, anger, and danger.

upright.tags: The Sun, The Heart, Number 5, Fire, Pride, Glory, Warpth, "Strength", "The Sun"
upright.description:
The fifth sign of the zodiac, Leo is a fixed fire sign, and this brash, courageous, headstrong lion rules the heart. Leo's dedication to its emotions and ideals can border on zealotry but is a card that sincerely concerned with matters of courage, honour, and pride. In tarot, Leo is associated with "The Sun" and "Strength" (its ruling planet being the sun), and much like the two major arcana cards it radiates optimism and tenacity.

Leo seeks to elevate itself to its highest potential, and reflects our need for recognition and gratitude. It can also suggest being burdened by one's ego and struggling with selfishness., and attempting to make room for others and their perspectives and dreams.

upright.tags: The Clouds, Shoulder Pole, Number 7, Venus, Equality, Indecision, The Scales, "Justice"
upright.description:
The seventh sign in the zodiac, Libra is a cardinal air sigh and governs the lower back, kidneys, and glutes - stabilizing the body. Ruled by the planet Venus, it is often associated with love and attachment, and is affiliated with the tarot card "Justice" - a direct contemporary to the scales of Libra. The carrying pole over the figure's shoulder turns them into a type of scale as they balance the contents, which is apt - Libra is entirely concerned with the nature of balance.

Libra is about resolving conflicts, perusing equality, and seeking reciprocal attachment. However, it can also be associated with indecision, as taking on too many perspectives can leave it incapable of drawing conclusions.

upright.tags: Sun, Moon, Stars, Number 0, Energy, Life, Warmth, Endless Possibility
upright.description:
The only means as by which mirrors reflect images is through the presence of light. The moon reflects the light of the sun as it does not produce any light of its own. The sun operates as our planet's primary source of light, and the warmth  by which all life is made possible. The light of the stars reaches us after thousands of years of travel, further reinforcing The Light's associations with momentum, life-affirming energy, and warmth.

The presence of this card is pervasive throughout the deck, and is intended to facilitate the ability to reflect upon the other cards - simultaneously casting light into out shadows, and making the presence of shadows possible.

upright.tags: Lychee, The Flesh, Numbers 43 and 7, Desire, Distance, Romance
upright.description: Longing is a state we embody in the physical world. As such, a hand of flesh - not bone - holds onto a stem of lychee, a fruit typically associated with love, desire and desire. What we wish for is so often here, in the material world, but this card asks us to investigate our other desires as well. The fruit may rot and the flesh may rend from bone, but what of the longing? Do we long for material items, romance, family, friendship? Glory, status, or acknowledgement? How does it motivate us, and to what end? This card can imply distance, deep-seated love, and loneliness. It can also suggest superficiality, materialism, and delusion.

upright.tags: Swallowtail Butterflies, Numbers 16 and 7, Communication, Acceptance, Openness
upright.description:
The butterfly has long been associated with change, hope, and growth. Swallowtail butterflies in particular have been linked with communication between our world and that of the spirits and the dead. The Messengers inquires as to whether one is open, receptive, and willing to interpret the signs being relayed to them, for one's personal or spiritual growth. What forces are at work around us? What signs have been relayed? What changes need to be made in one's life, and how does instinct play into what needs to be done?
This card calls us to pay attention to signs, symbols, and patterns in our lives. It can also imply we are ignoring overt messages or being willfully ignorant.

upright.tags: House Crows, Smoke, The Moon, Numbers 20 and 2, Uncertainty, A Lack of Clarity
upright.description: Miasma explores that which clouds and distorts our vision. A myriad of things can limit our understanding of situations, people, and circumstances, and our vision can become further distorted as the obstacles in our path continue to mount. This fog is temporary, however, and will lift - it is a matter of patience, watching, and waiting. This card suggests a need to break away, reconvene, and seek truth. It can also suggest gross oversights, misinterpretation, and gullibility. One must be careful not to fall victim to the clouded images in their wake.

upright.tags: Anemone, Numbers 31 and 4, Illusions, Disorted Vision
upright.description:
The Mirage asks us questions about the illusions of this world. The smoke and mirrors of this life shroud reality that we and the others around us experience. What is real? What is fabricated? To what degree do we engage in fabrication in order to lead a very specific kind of life? Flowers bust forward from the eye-sockets of the skull depicted, painting a very specific picture. The anemones depicted in the card open in the morning and close at night, much like blinking - what do we miss when our eyes are closed?

This card explores our relationship to the truth, and the ways in which we can distort, shift, and pull away from it. It can also suggest deception.

upright.tags: The Mirror, Numbers 49 -13- and 4, Reflection, Contemplation
upright.description: The final card of the oracle deck, The Mirror has reflected all things made visible by "The Light" - card zero to card forty-nine. It asks us to consider our energy, actions, thoughts, and to meditate upon past circumstances in our eyes that impact us in the present. A mirror affords us the opportunity to see the passage of time, and reflections act as a portal. Today, the mirror and its reflections have cemented themselves in our lives more than ever; we must ask ourselves how do we operate within their confines. How do we function with image, idolatry, vanity and introspection? This card focuses on the deep-seated need for contemplation and reflection. It can also imply illusion, inversion, and obsession.

upright.tags: Water, The Child, Numbers 30 and 3, Nurturing, Creation, The Elements of Water and Earth,
upright.description:
The figure of The Mother cradles a child in their arms while sitting in water, gazing long in the distance as if assessing for the child's safety. This card is associated with the elements of water and earth, the primary providers of life on our planet. It explores themes of nurturing, protection, sacred knowledge, creation, invention, transformation, and patience. 

This card is deeply associated with the passage of time, and encourages us to take note of time's transitions and the stages we pass through over the course of our lives. In what ways do we evolve and grow?

upright.tags: The Moon, Wisteria, Numbers 37 - 10 - and 1,Grief, Burden, "The Tower"
upright.description: The Mourners card is associated with the tarot card "The Tower". Much like "The Tower", The Mourners asks us questions about the nature of the calamity and grief. It isn't just individuals that we mourn - we also mourn phases of our lives, the person we once were, and the life paths we have diverged from. Mourning is an individual and private experience for many, but it is important to take hold of one another in order to lessen the burden of our grief. The Mourners hold on to one another in direct juxtaposition to "The Dancers". The Mourners are entwined with each other as though they were one. This card asks us questions about the role grief plays in our lives. It can also suggest suffering, confusion, and loneliness.

upright.tags: Water, Cupped Skull as Vessel, Numbers 15 and 6, Forgiveness, Truth-Seeking, The Suit of Cups
upright.description: Offerings is associated with the suit of cups and the element of water. This card navigates the nature of ritual, forgiveness, the pursuit of the truth, and the ask of requesting assistance and fortune. What are the many trades and exchanges that we offer to ourselves, the universe, and others in the pursuit of what we desire? What must be given or relinquished in order to change our circumstances? It is important to humble oneself before requesting anything of the universe. This card suggests a need to release - habits, items, ego, or individuals. It can also suggest a need to pay homage and express gratitude for all that one has, and ensure that we do not take our good fortune for granted.

upright.tags: The Cane, The Path, The Moon, Numbers 19 and 20, Journeys, Foresight,
upright.description: A figure stands at the end of a winding path, gazing into the distance as the moon shines overhead. This card follows "The Gate", implying the traveler has made it past their initial barriers. Now all that remains is a long road ahead and the many forks and choices that follow. What is it that we're seeking? Is the road ahead easy, or will we find ourselves transversing even more obstacles? While the future can be uncertain, the path laid before us implies others have walked it before. The Path is a card that concerns itself with the art of projection and foresight. It can also imply overanalyzing, catastrophizing, or finding oneself paralyzed by possibilities.

upright.tags: Luna Moth, The Moon, Numbers 24 and 6, Transformation, Cycles
upright.description:
Like the moon, many things in our lives operate in cycles as they change. For some, these cycles are predictable, timely, and orderly. For others, they can be so erratic they are not even viewed as cyclical unless one takes the time to step back and observe the patterns taking place. Some cycles can feel cruel in how brief they are; the luna moth lives approximately a week as an adult and does not feed in this time, laying their eggs and breeding before passing away. What are the phases of our lives, and what new transitions do we find ourselves in the midst of now?
Phases reminds us that we are always transforming. It can also suggest that we are not making room for the natural order of things.

upright.tags: Twin Fish, The Sea, The Moon, Numbers 12 and 3, Water, Contemplation, Neptune, "The Moon"
upright.description:
The twelfth and final sign of the zodiac, Pisces is a mutable water sign, associated with the planet Neptune. In tarot, it governs "The Moon" card, and on the human body it rules the feet. Pisces is a culmination of the astrological cycle, and as a result this card is very introspective. The twin fish imply an ability to harmoniously contain multitudes, while also being in perpetual motion with one another. They also exhibit a high sensitivity and deep empathy for all that has come before them. 

Pisces requests we recognize the many lessons in the life cycle, and patiently keep our minds and hearts open too synthesize our dreams and sensitivities. It can also imply pessimism and aimless wandering.

upright.tags: The Palm, The Eye, The Halo, Numbers 34 and 7, Seeking Help and Truth, Need
upright.description: The Plea is a card concerned with our relationship to that which we ask of ourselves, others, and the universe. The palm reaches upward, haloed, while the eye suggests a need to be discerning of what one wishes for. What are our desires? What remains just out of reach? What are the things we require above all else in order to find ourselves at peace, and how are we working toward those things mentally, physically, and spiritually? In times of great pain or struggle, what do we ask for? What do we need? This card can imply a desire to reach out to others to seek help, fulfillment, and support. It can also suggest overreacting, begging, and impairing oneself.

upright.tags: Halo, Stars, Tiled Floor into Infinity, Numbers 13 and 4, Higher Thinking, Foucs, Intention
upright.description: The Prayer asks us to take stock of what we consider worthy of worship. This card focuses on the nature of intention, elevating our bodies and minds spiritually and physically, and noting the things we ask of the universe, divinity, and each other. To what do we pray and set intentions? What do we revere and consider greater than ourselves? What is the nature of the things we ask for: protection, love, warmth, forgiveness, wealth? The floor of the card stretches to infinity, and we find the possibilities of growth and change are endless as a result. This card is associated with power, reverence, and humility. It can also imply selfishness and greed.

upright.tags: The Peacock, Numbers 26 and 8, Esteem, Power, Beauty, Arrogance
upright.description: The peacock is widely associated with pride in many cultures. In Asian folklore it is said that despite its great beauty, the peacock has "ugly" feet, and the bird despairs over them every time it gazes down at them. A symbol of beauty, esteem, wisdom, and power, the peacock is also commonly associated with arrogance and short-sightedness. What does our pride blind us to? What facets of ourselves do we ignore? To what degree are we victims of our own egos? This card navigates our relationship with pride. How can it benefit and fortify us, and in what ways might it make us more prone to oversights due to arrogance and ignorance?

upright.tags: Candles, Flame, Sunflowers, Numbers 46 - 10- and 1, The Suit of Wands, Element of Fire, Growth
upright.description: Radiance concerns itself with warmth, acceptance and growth. In tarot, it is associated with the suit of wands., sand as such, Radiance retains the ambitious, fiery persistent energy of the suit. Radiance glows outwards and casts its light upon all that we touch. In what ways can we extend our warmth, gratitude, and ambitions to the circumstances and individuals in our lives? This card is associated with creation, manifestation, and positivity. It can also imply carelessness and a near-foolish amount of optimism.

upright.tags: Black-Naped Hare, Intenstines, Blood, Numbers 38 - 11- and 2, "The Hanged Man"
upright.description: The black-naped hare looks sightlessly into the distance.The end of life affords us visions no other experience can, and these visions are endured by the individual alone. The Sacrifice explores the things we must sever, cull, and change in order to move forward from one life to the next. As we distance ourselves from the previous state of being, we are able to see what once was with new eyes and clarity. This card requests that we reprioritize, take stock of whats present, what will remain, and what must be removed in order to move forward. This card implies a need to grow, transform,and submit. It can also imply martyrdom, mutiny, and a disregard for oneself and others.

upright.tags: The Bow and Arrow, Flames, Number 9, Fire, Dedication, Novelty, Jupiter, "Temperance"
upright.description:
The ninth sign of the zodiac, Sagittarius is a mutable fire sign and is ruled by the planet Jupiter. On the body, Sagittarius governs the thighs and legs, and that is reflected in the nature of the sign; perpetually moving and propelling itself -forward when it comes to new ideas and ventures. In tarot, it is associated with the "Temperance" card as they are both deeply philosophical and novel, constantly in flux like the liquid that pours back and forth from "Temperance's" cup. Dynamic and ready to strike, Sagittarius pulls back its arrow and narrows its focus.

Sagittarius concerns itself with movement, flow, and dynamism. It also can suggest a need to slow down, reevaluate, and rest.

upright.tags: Scythe, Scorpion's Tail, Lotus, Water, Number 8, Mars, Pluto, Transformation, "Death"
upright.description:
The eighth sign of the zodiac, Scorpio is a fixed water sign and rules the pelvis, hips, and reproductive system. It is governed by the planets Mars and Pluto, and is most closely associated with the "Death" tarot card. While Scorpio and "Death" are both formidable and intimidating at times, this card is truly most concerned with the art of transformation. Scorpio creates, destroys, and reinvents. Like the lotus present on the card, beauty and new growth rises from the mire and mess of life.

Scorpio seeks to take inventory of what is present in its life, what must be retained, and what must be culled. Being a card of transformation, Scorpio sternly acknowledges that we must change.

upright.tags: Orb Spider, Web, Files, Numbers 44 and 8, Entrapment, Stagnation
upright.description: The orb spider traps unwitting flies in its web, dooming victims to the cold inevitability of death. The Snare asks us to reflect upon our roadblocks, the things we feel trapped by, and the roles we feel we cannot break free of. What limitations have we set upon ourselves, and how have they made us stagnate? What fears and anxieties stop us in our tracks and prevent ourselves from feeling as if we can move forward? How threatening are these snares - which are grounded in reality, and which are exaggerated? This card suggests the feeling of being confined in one space or mindset, or or halted in one's progress. It can also suggest sabotage, deceit, and being driven into a corner.

upright.tags: The Sword, Numbers 35 and 8, Planning, Conquering, Vitality
upright.description: Sitting at quiet ease, The Soldier is contemplative, composed, and patient. While the Soldier has the opportunity to enact great violence, it is at the discretion of that which directs them. From who do we take our orders and directives? Do we defer to our egos, our superiors, or something greater and far more obscure? The Soldier is, in this fashion, an extension of that which commands it. Who is in control? This card suggests a need for authority, structure, stability, and a desire to move forward with clear direction. It can also imply suppression and confinement.

upright.tags: The Lotus, The Rabab, Numbers 47 -11 - and 2, Rhythm, Motion
upright.description:
Often when we think of the universe, we first think of light- but there is also song. The Song brings the idea of universal sound and rhythm into the forefront. What are the sounds that permeate our spaces and our minds? What is our inner dialogue relaying to us? In the absence of other sounds, humans will hear the inner workings of their body. What is the steady beat of our heart trying to tell us?
The Song asks us to focus on our surroundings, and the things in motion producing sound around us at all times. Much like absolute darkness, absolute silence is incredibly hard to find. We are never quite alone.

upright.tags: The Sword, The Clouds, Numbers 22 and 4, Struggle, The Suit of Swords, The Element of Air
upright.description:
Strife is closely associated with the suit of swords and the element of air. The figure envelopes their arms around themselves, their spine replaced with a blade, implying that our struggles are not just external, but internal. What do we find ourselves grappling with? What brings us into the midst of conflict pain, frustration, and misunderstanding, and how do we navigate these trials?
It is inevitable that we will all experience a variety of emotions, struggles, and discord in our lives, so it is best to recognize who we are and who we want to be should conflict arise. This card can also suggest inner struggle, pessimism, and tension.

upright.tags: Dagger, Coins, Cup, Branch, Numbers 17 and 8,The Tarot Suits of Cups Wands Swords and Pentacles,
upright.description: All four suits of the tarot are present in this card.As such, Talismans is an amalgamation of the four elements associated with the suits: earth, water, fire, and air. Talismans are often associated with protection, but they are also symbols intended to convey very specific messages. What things do we pull towards us to provide protection and comfort? What empowers us? What in our vicinity or on our person serves as a reminder of who we are and how we must live? This card asks us meditate on what people, objects, or beliefs we hold close to our hearts and seek out when we are in need. It can also imply an over-attachment to idols and a need to pursue self-reliance and power.

upright.tags: The Horns, The Throat, Bramble, Number 2, Venus, Earth, The Bull, Loyality, "The Hieorphant"
upright.description:
The second sign of the Zodiac, Taurus is a fixed earth sign. Taurus rules the throat, and is known for strong, steadfast values and an unwavering commitment to its own values. Taurus is a creature of the earth, and therefore grounded to the affairs of the world. Much like its ruling planet, Venus, it pursues love, beauty, and serenity. Much like "The Hieorphant" of tarot, Taurus is a teacher.

Taurus can be interpreted as encouraging individuals to consider their values and dive deep into their structure and significance. It can also be associated with a stubborn commitment to ideals, and an unwillingness to embrace change.

upright.tags: The Arms, Numbers 25 and 7, Suit of Rings, The Earth Element, Attachment
upright.description: Tethers questions us about our relationship with attachment. As it is associated with the earth and the tarot suit of rings, Tethers concerns itself with earthly matters such as the state of our relationships with life and this world. What are the things that keep us grounded? Inversely, what are the attachments that can impede our spiritual development - our pride, greed, fear or caution? This card implies a need to interrogate what we consider fundamentally important in our lives and what tethers us to this reality. It also requests that we make room for the ability to detach and be more objective in our perspectives.

upright.tags: The Bluejay, Earring, Numbers 39 -12 - and 3, Misunderstanding, "The Hermit"
upright.description: While birds are associated with stealing shiny, valuable objects in folklore, these beliefs are largely unsubstantiated in reality, or misunderstood. The Thief invites us to investigate our prejudices, misunderstandings, miscommunications, and our interactions with myth - how a story can become larger than reality itself, and proliferate so widely that none question it. In tarot, it is associated with "The Hermit" - an oft misunderstood card that asks us to examine our relationship with introversion, reclusion, and solitary thought. This card can suggest miscommunication, breakdowns in hierarchy, and illusions. It can also symbolize loss, deception, and an absence of control.

upright.tags: Chain Viper, Northern Goshawk, Numbers 14 and 5, Bravery, Resolve, Danger Taking Charge,
upright.description:
The northern goshawk has widely been considered a symbol of bravery, valour, and camaraderie. In its talons it holds a chain viper, the chain having its associations with the traditional tarot card "The Devil". While "The Devil" is often associated with vice, Valour asks us to explore how we confront temptation, cowardice, and stagnation. Who or what helps us to rise to the occasion? What inspires courage and nobility within us? When we must confront our enemies and our fears, who do we become and who do we aspire to be? 
This card explores themes of confrontation and bringing oneself to do the right thing in the face of adversity and pain. It can also imply pride and self-righteousness.

upright.tags: The Sehra, The Groom, Numbers 40 and 4, The Evil Eye, Protection
upright.description: The sehra is a veil often made of garlands of flowers or pearls. It is tied in a way that hides the face of the groom from his intended; it also provides protection from nazar (the evil eye). The veil in this card explores a notion of hiding - what is concealed and treasured? For what reasons? What impact can the gaze of others have on our security and wellbeing? What precautions must be taken? The Veil can imply approaching new tasks and opportunities under a cover of sorts - working through one's thoughts and pursuits in private, and finding fulfillment without the opinions and recognition of others. It can also suggest clouded vision, isolation, danger, and fear.

upright.tags: The Maiden, Wheat, Number 6, Earth, Mercury, Logic, Structure, Control, "The Hermit"
upright.description:
The sixth sign of the zodiac, Virgo is a mutable earth sign ruled by Mercury, and it governs the digestive system and abdomen. Much like the tarot card it's closely associated with, "The Hermit", Virgo often seeks solitude in order too engage in deep-seated contemplation and intellectual pursuits. Like the inner workings of the body, Virgo seeks sophisticated structure and logic to operate at its best capacity. This card asks us to take stock of the systems present in our lives, and the phases that must come to pass as time marches on.

Virgo wishes to bring stability and serenity into our lives, but it can come at the expense of cool detachment, or a near impassive approach to what it perceives as inevitable.

upright.tags: The Eye, Clouds, Numbers 41 and 5, Clarity, Empathy, Inevitbility
upright.description:
Visions looks back with a single point of view. It sees past the clouding effects of ego, pride, and envy, and evenly returns our gaze; steadfast and perfect. The clouds part and light radiates, having seen through the fog into what we know to be real. This card not only relays the act of seeing, but the act of looking inward and knowing. What truths do we hide from, knowing they make life difficult to confront who we are and what we must do? What messages are being relayed to us?
This card explores themes of clarity, mental acuity, and reality. It can also imply inability - gazing long into what we do not want to acknowledge, but know to be true in our hearts.
